name: Orchid (Crayola)
lede: Orchid is a soft pink-purple that Crayola has sold under that name since 1958, after nine years as "Medium Red-Violet."

sections.title: A flower name that replaced a mixing label
sections.body:
Crayola introduced this hue in its crayon boxes in 1949 under a plainly descriptive name, Medium Red-Violet; from 1958 the same color has been sold as Orchid, after the flower family, which Wikipedia's crayon history lists as the same color under a new name [1]. Unlike many Crayola colors, it has stayed in the lineup ever since, without a retirement [1]. Our sources carry no further record of why the flower name was chosen over the older descriptive one [1].

The nearest named look-alikes on file are [[rose-purple|Rose-Purple]], almost the same shade, and [[kobi|Kobi]] and [[mallow-pink|Mallow Pink]], both redder [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A close match to this pink-purple turns up in only 1 of our 23,781 archived paintings, about 0.004 per cent, rarer than 88 per cent of our named colors [3]. A sample of one painting is too small to support any claim beyond its bare existence, and these are photographs of an aged, varnished canvas, not a pigment test [3].

questions.q: What was Crayola's Orchid crayon originally called, before its 1958 renaming?
True or false: Crayola has retired its Orchid crayon at least once since 1949.

openers: Crayola's Orchid has never been retired since 1949, under one name or the other.
